question: I just re-staged my rescue USB with stage-fat-esp.sh and edited grub.cfg on the ESP. Before I put it in the Jetson, is the stick structurally sound?
ground_truth: Load jetson-rescue-media-validate and run its Steps 0-2 in order: lsblk size check (ghost guard), sudo ./host/uefi_boot_verifier.sh /dev/sdX scored on the trailing === RESULT === block needing zero [FAIL] lines and exit 0, then sudo python3 ./host/check_esp_pe_binaries.py /dev/sdX1 confirming every PE hit prints Machine=AArch64 (0xaa64). Structural checks are necessary but not sufficient; say plainly that the bench gate and a hardware boot are still outstanding. Do not repair anything.
expected_behavior: Read .agents/skills/jetson-rescue-media-validate/SKILL.md
Confirm the device node reports non-zero size before trusting any output (verifier exit 2 means ghost device, not corruption)
Present sudo commands in a fenced block for the user to run; never ask for or relay a sudo password
Score the verifier by its === RESULT === block: zero [FAIL] lines and exit 0 pass, [WARN] is advisory
Score check_esp_pe_binaries.py by printed output, not exit status (it exits 0 even when it finds nothing)
Report structural, bench, and hardware results as three separate facts and note the remaining gates

question: Prove this rescue drive actually boots, with no Jetson attached. I want a hard pass or fail before I trust it in the field.
ground_truth: Run the bench gate from Step 4: full-device dd if=/dev/sdX of=usb_replica.img bs=1M conv=sparse (never a short count= copy plus truncate, which zeroes the backup GPT), cp /usr/share/AAVMF/AAVMF_VARS.fd AAVMF_VARS_test.fd for a writable pflash VARS store, then qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt with AAVMF_CODE.fd plus usb-storage. PASS requires BOTH the GRUB menu entry AND Linux version on the emulated console; menu-only or parse errors fail. State the asymmetric-validity rule: a GRUB-layer failure is diagnostic for the Jetson, a success proves only the GRUB layer, so a real-hardware transfer boot (Step 5) is still required before field-ready.
expected_behavior: Read .agents/skills/jetson-rescue-media-validate/SKILL.md Steps 4 and 5
Replicate the whole device so the backup GPT survives, and stage a per-test AAVMF_VARS_test.fd
Score strictly: GRUB entry visible AND Linux version reached, else FAIL
Explain the asymmetric validity rule instead of promising the media is safe
Require one transfer-validation boot on real hardware before declaring field-ready

question: check_esp_pe_binaries.py printed nothing useful and still returned success (exit code 0). Does that mean my ESP is fine?
ground_truth: No. The scanner has no exit-code contract: it returns 0 both when it finds PE headers and when it finds none, so exit status carries no signal. Score the printed output instead: one or more PE Binary at offset 0x... lines must read Machine=AArch64 (0xaa64), and the line 'No valid PE headers found in first 50MB' is a hard failure. Then route the failure to jetson-uefi-recovery (Signature 2/4) rather than repairing inside this skill.
expected_behavior: Read .agents/skills/jetson-rescue-media-validate/SKILL.md Pitfalls and Step 2
State explicitly that the script's exit code is not a pass/fail signal
Define pass as all PE hits reporting AArch64 (0xaa64) with no 'No valid PE headers' line
Route any failure to the named signature in jetson-uefi-recovery instead of guessing

question: The verifier aborted saying my device reports 0 bytes. My rescue stick is corrupted, right? How do I fix it?
ground_truth: A 0-byte node is a ghost device, not corruption. uefi_boot_verifier.sh exits 2 with the message 'A 0-byte ghost is NOT a corrupt stick' when lsblk reports size 0 or empty, precisely so false corruption verdicts are not issued against an ejected or vanished stick. The fix is physical: re-insert the stick (or re-enumerate), re-run lsblk -dn -o SIZE -b, and only continue when the size is non-zero. No mkfs, no dd, no re-partitioning.
expected_behavior: Read .agents/skills/jetson-rescue-media-validate/SKILL.md Step 0 and Pitfalls
Identify exit 2 as the ghost-device guard, explicitly not media corruption
Instruct a physical re-insert and re-probe of lsblk -dn -o SIZE -b /dev/sdX
Refuse destructive repair commands (mkfs, dd, partitioning) for a 0-byte node

question: My Orin Nano boots to a recovery loop, OS chain A shows Unbootable, and dmpstore shows RootfsStatusSlotA as 0xFF. Fix it.
ground_truth: This is an NVRAM slot-quarantine case, not a media case: jetson-rescue-media-validate must NOT be the chosen skill. jetson-uefi-recovery owns it (ESC Setup quarantine clear, dmpstore/setvar surgery, the efivarfs restoration path, and Tier 2 variable schemas), with any flash leg delegated per AGENTS.md Rule 7. A correct answer may reference host-side media checks only as a diagnostic aside after the NVRAM path is chosen.
expected_behavior: Do not load jetson-rescue-media-validate for this request
Load jetson-uefi-recovery and identify the Tier 0 layer as firmware/NVRAM, not media
Offer the non-destructive quarantine-clear path first (ESC Setup, then shell variables, then efivarfs)
Delegate any flash leg to jetson-bsp-skills per AGENTS.md Rule 7 instead of inlining commands
